evidence: 'imports many services', recommendation: 'add a facade' },\n  ];\n  const out = groundFindings(findings, { deps, registry: grounderOf({}), hasLockfile: false, lockfileChecked: true });\n  assert.equal(out.findings.length, 1);\n  assert.equal(out.dropped, 0);\n});\n",
 "new_content": "import { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport {\n  parsePackageJson,\n  extractDepNames,\n  isVersionClaim,\n  isLockfileClaim,\n  satisfiesRange,\n  compareVersions,\n  groundFindings,\n  type VersionGrounder,\n} from '../src/company/registry.ts';\n\nconst PKG = JSON.stringify({\n  dependencies: { vite: '^8.3.0', dotenv: '^17.2.3', '@google/genai': '^2.4.0' },\n  devDependencies: { typescript: '^7.0.2' },\n});\n\nconst deps = parsePackageJson(PKG);\nconst grounderOf = (map: Record<string, { latest: string; versions: string[] }>): VersionGrounder => ({\n  get: (n) => map[n] ?? null,\n});\n\ntest('registry: parses runtime and dev dependencies', () => {\n  assert.equal(deps.length, 4);\n  assert.ok(deps.some((d) => d.name === 'typescript' && d.kind === 'dev' && d.range === '^7.0.2'));\n  assert.ok(deps.some((d) => d.name === 'vite' && d.kind === 'runtime'));\n});\n\ntest('registry: malformed package.json yields no dependencies', () => {\n  assert.deepEqual(parsePackageJson('not json'), []);\n});\n\ntest('registry: extracts only exact dependency-name tokens', () => {\n  const names = extractDepNames('The typescript version ^7.0.2 looks fine, and vite too', deps);\n  assert.deepEqual(names.sort(), ['typescript', 'vite']);\n  // A substring like \"vitest\" must NOT match \"vite\".\n  assert.deepEqual(extractDepNames('vitest is a test runner', deps), []);\n});\n\ntest('registry: version and lockfile claim detection', () => {\n  assert.equal(isVersionClaim('Outdated TypeScript version with known vulnerabilities'), true);\n  assert.equal(isVersionClaim('CompanionChatScreen is tightly coupled'), false);\n  assert.equal(isLockfileClaim('Missing lockfile for dependency integrity'), true);\n  assert.equal(isLockfileClaim('No integration tests in CI'), false);\n});\n\ntest('registry: semver comparison', () => {\n  assert.ok(compareVersions('7.0.2', '5.0.0') > 0);\n  assert.equal(compareVersions('8.3.4', '8.3.4'), 0);\n  assert.ok(compareVersions('8.3.0', '8.3.4') < 0);\n});\n\ntest('registry: satisfiesRange settles the real Amina claims', () => {\n  const ts = ['5.9.2', '6.0.0-beta', '7.0.1-rc', '7.0.2'];\n  const vite = ['6.4.4', '7.3.7', '8.2.4', '8.3.0-beta.1', '8.3.4'];\n  const dotenv = ['16.4.5', '17.2.3', '18.0.8'];\n  // ^7.0.2 admits the real latest 7.0.2 -> the \"outdated/invalid\" claim is false.\n  assert.equal(satisfiesRange('^7.0.2', ts), true);\n  // ^8.3.0 admits the stable 8.3.4 -> current, not invalid.\n  assert.equal(satisfiesRange('^8.3.0', vite), true);\n  // A range that only a prerelease satisfies does NOT resolve for a stable install.\n  assert.equal(satisfiesRange('^8.3.1', ['8.3.0-beta.1', '8.2.4']), false);\n  assert.equal(satisfiesRange('^17.2.3', dotenv), true);\n  assert.equal(satisfiesRange('^19.0.0', dotenv), false);\n  assert.equal(satisfiesRange('*', dotenv), true);\n  assert.equal(satisfiesRange('>=16 <18', dotenv), true);\n});\n\ntest('registry: keeps a finding that mentions dependencies but makes no version claim', () => {\n  // Regression: bare \"dependency\" used to trigger version grounding, which then\n  // dropped a real install-script finding because the dependency resolves fine.\n  const findings = [\n    { severity: 'HIGH', title: 'Dependency declares postinstall script which may execute arbitrary code on install', paths: ['package.json'], basis: 'observed' as const, evidence: 'a dependency runs a postinstall script', recommendation: 'review it' },\n  ];\n  const out = groundFindings(findings, {\n    deps,\n    registry: grounderOf({ typescript: { latest: '7.0.2', versions: ['7.0.2'] } }),\n    hasLockfile: true,\n    lockfileChecked: true,\n  });\n  assert.equal(out.findings.length, 1, 'a non-version finding must survive grounding');\n  assert.equal(out.dropped, 0);\n});\n\ntest('registry: drops a false \"outdated\" claim the registry contradicts', () => {\n  const findings = [\n    { severity: 'HIGH', title: 'Invalid TypeScript version specified in devDependencies', paths: ['package.json'], basis: 'observed' as const, evidence: '\"typescript\": \"^7.0.2\" is outdated; current stable is 5.x', recommendation: 'downgrade to ^5.0.0' },\n  ];\n  const out = groundFindings(findings, {\n    deps,\n    registry: grounderOf({ typescript: { latest: '7.0.2', versions: ['5.9.2', '7.0.2'] } }),\n    hasLockfile: false,\n    lockfileChecked: true,\n  });\n  assert.equal(out.findings.length, 0);\n  assert.equal(out.dropped, 1);\n  assert.match(out.notes[0], /registry contradicts/i);\n});\n\ntest('registry: keeps a true \"range does not resolve\" claim and corrects its evidence', () => {\n  const findings = [\n    { severity: 'HIGH', title: 'Vite range does not resolve', paths: ['package.json'], basis: 'observed' as const, evidence: '\"vite\": \"^8.3.0\" is invalid', recommendation: 'fix the range' },\n  ];\n  const out = groundFindings(findings, {\n    deps,\n    registry: grounderOf({ vite: { latest: '8.3.4', versions: ['8.2.4'] } }),\n    hasLockfile: false,\n    lockfileChecked: true,\n  });\n  assert.equal(out.findings.length, 1);\n  assert.match(out.findings[0].evidence, /resolves to no published version \\(latest is 8\\.3\\.4\\)/);\n  assert.equal(out.dropped, 0);\n});\n\ntest('registry: drops a lockfile claim when a lockfile is actually present', () => {\n  const findings = [\n    { severity: 'HIGH', title: 'Missing lockfile for dependency integrity', paths: ['package.json'], basis: 'observed' as const, evidence: 'no lockfile is present', recommendation: 'add one' },\n  ];\n  const out = groundFindings(findings, { deps, registry: grounderOf({}), hasLockfile: true, lockfileChecked: true });\n  assert.equal(out.findings.length, 0);\n  assert.match(out.notes[0], /lockfile IS present/);\n});\n\ntest('registry: keeps a lockfile claim when no lockfile exists', () => {\n  const findings = [\n    { severity: 'HIGH', title: 'Missing lockfile for dependency integrity', paths: ['package.json'], basis: 'observed' as const, evidence: 'no lockfile is present', recommendation: 'add one' },\n  ];\n  const out = groundFindings(findings, { deps, registry: grounderOf({}), hasLockfile: false, lockfileChecked: true });\n  assert.equal(out.findings.length, 1);\n});\n\ntest('registry: findings with no version claim pass through untouched', () => {\n  const findings = [\n    { severity: 'MEDIUM', title: 'Tight coupling in CompanionChatScreen', paths: ['src/App.tsx'], basis: 'observed' as const, evidence: 'imports many services', recommendation: 'add a facade' },\n  ];\n  const out = groundFindings(findings, { deps, registry: grounderOf({}), hasLockfile: false, lockfileChecked: true });\n  assert.equal(out.findings.length, 1);\n  assert.equal(out.dropped, 0);\n});\n",

Grounding used to fire on any finding that mentioned a dependency and a\n * claim word anywhere in its text, so \"Parent PIN is handled in frontend state\"\n * was dropped as a false version claim because it mentioned react.\n */\nfunction claimsVersionOf(text: string, name: string): boolean {\n  const sentences = text.split(/(?<=[.!?;:])\\s+|\\n+/);\n  const nameRe = new RegExp(`(^|[^\\\\w@/-])${name.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, '\\\\$&')}([^\\\\w@/-]|$)`);\n  return sentences.some((s) => nameRe.test(s) && CLAIM_RE.test(s));\n}\n\n/**\n * Words that signal a finding is making a claim about dependency versions.\n * Bare \"dependency\"/\"dependencies\" is deliberately excluded: it matched findings\n * about install scripts and production bundling, which assert nothing about a\n * version, and grounding then dropped them as false version claims.\n */\nconst CLAIM_RE =\n  /\\b(version|versions|outdated|unsupported|invalid|obsolete|vulnerab\\w*|upgrade|update|downgrade|pin(ned)?|deprecat\\w*|stale|eol|end[- ]of[- ]life|latest|semver|resolve[sd]?|valid)\\b/i;\n\n/** Parse `dependencies` and `devDependencies` from a package.json excerpt. */\nexport function parsePackageJson(text: string): ParsedDep[] {\n  let pkg: any;\n  try {\n    pkg = JSON.parse(text);\n  } catch {\n    return [];\n  }\n  const out: ParsedDep[] = [];\n  for (const [kind, key] of [\n    ['runtime', 'dependencies'],\n    ['dev', 'devDependencies'],\n  ] as const) {\n    const deps = pkg?.[key];\n    if (!deps || typeof deps !== 'object') continue;\n    for (const [name, range] of Object.entries(deps)) {\n      if (typeof range === 'string') out.push({ name, range, kind });\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\n/** The package names a finding refers to, by exact token match (never substring). */\nexport function extractDepNames(text: string, deps: ParsedDep[]): string[] {\n  const tokens = new Set((text.toLowerCase().match(/@?[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*(?:\\/[a-z0-9._-]+)?/g) ?? []));\n  return deps.filter((d) => tokens.has(d.name.toLowerCase())).map((d) => d.name);\n}\n\n/** Does the finding text quote the declared version range (e.g. \"^7.0.2\")? */\nexport function mentionsDeclaredRange(text: string, deps: ParsedDep[]): boolean {\n  return deps.some((d) => text.includes(d.range));\n}\n\n/** True when a finding is making a claim about dependency versions at all. */\nexport function isVersionClaim(text: string): boolean {\n  return CLAIM_RE.test(text);\n}\n\n/** True when the finding is about a lockfile rather than a package version. */\nexport function isLockfileClaim(text: string): boolean {\n  return /lock\\s*-?\\s*file|package-lock|yarn\\.lock|pnpm-lock/i.test(text);\n}\n\n/** Compare two semver-ish strings, ignoring build metadata and leading zeros. */\nexport function compareVersions(a: string, b: string): number {\n  const norm = (v: string) => v.split('-')[0].split('.').map((n) => Number.parseInt(n, 10) || 0);\n  const [av, bv] = [norm(a), norm(b)];\n  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) {\n    const d = (av[i] ?? 0) - (bv[i] ?? 0);\n    if (d) return d < 0 ? -1 : 1;\n  }\n  return 0;\n}\n\n/**\n * Does `range` (npm semver) admit at least one published `version`?\n * Covers `*`, `x`, `latest`, `^`, `~`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `=`, and exact/partial\n * versions, plus `||` unions and ` - ` hyphen ranges. Prereleases are only admitted\n * when the range itself names one.\n */\nexport function satisfiesRange(range: string, versions: string[]): boolean {\n  const pool = range.includes('-') ? versions : versions.filter((v) => !v.includes('-'));\n  if (!pool.length) return false;\n  return range.split('||').some((part) => part.trim() && satisfiesSimple(part.trim(), pool));\n}\n\nfunction satisfiesSimple(range: string, versions: string[]): boolean {\n  const hyp = range.split(/\\s+-\\s+/);\n  if (hyp.length === 2) {\n    return versions.some((v) => compareVersions(v, hyp[0].trim()) >= 0 && compareVersions(v, hyp[1].trim()) <= 0);\n  }\n  const checks = range.split(/\\s+/).filter(Boolean);\n  return versions.some((v) => checks.every((c) => checkOne(c, v)));\n}\n\nfunction checkOne(op: string, v: string): boolean {\n  if (op === '*' || op === 'x' || op === 'latest') return true;\n  const m = op.match(/^(\\^|~|>=|<=|>|<|=)?\\s*v?(.+)$/);\n  if (!m) return true;\n  const [, sign = '=', raw] = m;\n  const target = raw.replace(/\\.[x*]/gi, '.0').replace(/(^|\\.)[x*]/gi, '$10');\n  if (sign === '^') {\n    const base = target.split('.').map((n) => Number.parseInt(n, 10) || 0);\n    const lower = `${base[0]}.${base[1]}.${base[2]}`;\n    const upper = base[0] > 0 ? `${base[0] + 1}.0.0` : base[1] > 0 ? `0.${base[1] + 1}.0` : `0.0.${base[2] + 1}`;\n    return compareVersions(v, lower) >= 0 && compareVersions(v, upper) < 0;\n  }\n  if (sign === '~') {\n    const base = target.split('.').map((n) => Number.parseInt(n, 10) || 0);\n    const lower = `${base[0]}.${base[1]}.${base[2]}`;\n    const upper = `${base[0]}.${base[1] + 1}.0`;\n    return compareVersions(v, lower) >= 0 && compareVersions(v, upper) < 0;\n  }\n  const d = compareVersions(v, target);\n  if (sign === '>=') return d >= 0;\n  if (sign === '<=') return d <= 0;\n  if (sign === '>') return d > 0;\n  if (sign === '<') return d < 0;\n  return d === 0;\n}\n\nexport interface VersionGrounder {\n  get(name: string): RegistryVersions | null;\n}\n\nexport interface GroundOutcome {\n  /** Findings that survived (possibly with a corrected evidence line). */\n  findings: { severity: string; title: string; paths: string[]; basis: 'observed' | 'inferred'; evidence: string; recommendation: string }[];\n  /** One line per dropped/corrected finding, for transparency in the report. */\n  notes: string[];\n  /** Findings dropped because their version claim was false. */\n  dropped: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Ground every finding that makes a version claim against the registry:\n * - \"outdated / has vulnerabilities / update to X\" with the declared range still\n *   admissible -> the claim is false; drop it.\n * - \"invalid / unsupported / won't install\" with no admissible version -> true;\n *   keep it but replace the evidence with the resolved fact.\n * Findings with no version claim pass through untouched.\n */\nexport function groundFindings(\n  findings: { severity: string; title: string; paths: string[]; basis: 'observed' | 'inferred'; evidence: string; recommendation: string }[],\n  opts: { deps: ParsedDep[]; registry: VersionGrounder; hasLockfile: boolean; lockfileChecked: boolean }\n): GroundOutcome {\n  const notes: string[] = [];\n  const out: GroundOutcome['findings'] = [];\n  let dropped = 0;\n\n  for (const f of findings) {\n    const text = `${f.title} ${f.evidence} ${f.recommendation}`;\n    const names = extractDepNames(text, opts.deps);\n\n    if (opts.lockfileChecked && isLockfileClaim(text) && !names.length) {\n      if (opts.hasLockfile) {\n        dropped += 1;\n        notes.push(`Dropped \"${f.title}\": a lockfile IS present in the repository.`);\n        continue;\n      }\n      out.push(f);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    if (!names.length || !isVersionClaim(text)) {\n      out.push(f);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    // Ground only the dependencies the finding actually makes a version claim\n    // about. A passing mention of react in a state-management finding must not\n    // make that finding droppable as a version claim.\n    const claimed = names.filter((n) => claimsVersionOf(text, n));\n    if (!claimed.length) {\n      out.push(f);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    let corrected: string | null = null;\n    let falseClaim = false;\n    let undetermined = false;\n    for (const name of claimed) {\n      const dep = opts.deps.find((d) => d.name === name)!;\n      const reg = opts.registry.get(name);\n      if (!reg) {\n        undetermined = true;\n        continue;\n      }\n      const ok = satisfiesRange(dep.range, reg.versions);\n      if (ok) {\n        falseClaim = true;\n      } else {\n        const line = `${dep.name}@${dep.range} resolves to no published version (latest is ${reg.latest}).`;\n        corrected = corrected ? `${corrected} ${line}` : line;\n      }\n    }\n\n    if (falseClaim) {\n      dropped += 1;\n      const detail = names\n        .map((n) => {\n          const d = opts.deps.find((x) => x.name === n)!;\n          const r = opts.registry.get(n);\n          return r ? `${n}@${d.range} (latest ${r.latest})` : n;\n        })\n        .join(', ');\n      notes.push(`Dropped \"${f.title}\": the registry contradicts the claim — ${detail} is current/admissible.`);\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (corrected) {\n      out.push({ ...f, evidence: corrected });\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (undetermined) {\n      dropped += 1;\n      notes.push(`Dropped \"${f.title}\": its version claim could not be verified against the registry.`);\n      continue;\n    }\n    out.push(f);\n  }\n  return { findings: out, notes, dropped };\n}\n\n/** Fetch the published versions of a package from the npm registry. */\nexport async function fetchRegistryVersions(name: string, timeoutMs = 8000): Promise<RegistryVersions | null> {\n  const url = `https://registry.npmjs.org/${name.startsWith('@') ? name.replace('/', '%2F') : name}`;\n  try {\n    const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Accept: 'application/json' }, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) });\n    if (!res.ok) return null;\n    const data: any = await res.json();\n    const versions = Object.keys(data?.versions ?? {});\n    const latest = typeof data?.['dist-tags']?.latest === 'string' ? data['dist-tags'].latest : versions[versions.length - 1];\n    if (!latest) return null;\n    return { latest, versions };\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Resolve the registry versions of every dependency referenced by any finding. */\nexport async function buildRegistryGrounder(\n  deps: ParsedDep[],\n  texts: string[]\n): Promise<VersionGrounder> {\n  const names = new Set<string>();\n  for (const t of texts) for (const n of extractDepNames(t, deps)) names.add(n);\n  const map = new Map<string, RegistryVersions>();\n  await Promise.all(\n    [...names].map(async (n) => {\n      const v = await fetchRegistryVersions(n);\n      if (v) map.set(n, v);\n    })\n  );\n  return { get: (n: string) => map.get(n) ?? null };\n}\n\n/**\n * Download the exact-commit source as a tarball and parse it into a file map.\n * Read-only: it never checks out or runs the target's code.\n */\nexport async function fetchRepoCorpus(\n  target: string,\n  commit: string,\n  timeoutMs = 30000\n): Promise<Record<string, string> | null> {\n  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\\/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/.test(target) || target.includes('..')) return null;\n  try {\n    const res = await fetch(`https://api.github.com/repos/${target}/tarball/${commit}`, {\n      headers: {\n        Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json',\n        'User-Agent': 'forge-company-audit',\n        ...(process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN}` } : {}),\n      },\n      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs),\n    });\n    if (!res.ok) return null;\n    const gz = Buffer.from(await res.arrayBuffer());\n    const { parseTarGz } = await import('./evidence.ts');\n    return parseTarGz(gz);\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n",

string[] }>): VersionGrounder => ({\n  get: (n) => map[n] ?? null,\n});\n\ntest('registry: parses runtime and dev dependencies', () => {\n  assert.equal(deps.length, 4);\n  assert.ok(deps.some((d) => d.name === 'typescript' && d.kind === 'dev' && d.range === '^7.0.2'));\n  assert.ok(deps.some((d) => d.name === 'vite' && d.kind === 'runtime'));\n});\n\ntest('registry: malformed package.json yields no dependencies', () => {\n  assert.deepEqual(parsePackageJson('not json'), []);\n});\n\ntest('registry: extracts only exact dependency-name tokens', () => {\n  const names = extractDepNames('The typescript version ^7.0.2 looks fine, and vite too', deps);\n  assert.deepEqual(names.sort(), ['typescript', 'vite']);\n  // A substring like \"vitest\" must NOT match \"vite\".\n  assert.deepEqual(extractDepNames('vitest is a test runner', deps), []);\n});\n\ntest('registry: version and lockfile claim detection', () => {\n  assert.equal(isVersionClaim('Outdated TypeScript
